h1:
Mookata, Korean BBQ
and Seafood Buffets in Phuket That Are Worth It
intro: A long, all-you-can-eat dinner is how locals in Phuket love to catch up — from charcoal mookata with the classic dome pan for under two hundred a head, to Korean BBQ in the malls, to seafood buffets that pile prawns, shellfish, crab and fish in front of you. We picked only the places that are actually open right now, sorted by value and type, so you can choose by budget and group size.

blocks.html: Grill buffets in Phuket fall roughly into three groups. The first is Thai-style charcoal mookata with the dome pan — the cheapest option, great for a casual meal with friends or a big group. The second is Korean- or Japanese-style grill and shabu in the malls — mid-range, but the marinated meats are good and there's usually sushi and sashimi on the side. The third is seafood buffets built around fresh prawns, shellfish, crab and fish — pricier, but you get the full haul from the sea. Below they're sorted by value and budget.

This ranking leans on value for money first, not just how fancy a place is. Prices are rough ranges pulled from restaurant pages and reviews and can change, so always check with the venue before you go — especially the hotel restaurants that only run their buffet on certain days.

items.name: Heng Heng Mookata Buffet
items.blurb: Classic charcoal mookata with the dome pan and a well-stocked spread — marinated pork, meatballs, fresh veg, drinks included. The cheapest on this list, and an easy pick when you just want to eat with friends and not think too hard about the budget.

items.name: Super Heng Mookata Buffet
items.blurb: All-you-can-eat mookata with no time limit and free-flow water. Plenty of lines to choose from — pork, seafood, veg — at a fair price. Great for settling in and chatting without anyone rushing you.

items.name: Chalong Buffet
items.blurb: In the Chalong area — classic charcoal mookata with the dome pan and a generous spread, all-you-can-eat with drinks included. Handy if you're staying around Chalong or Rawai and want to eat close to your hotel.

items.name: Suk Sabai Mookata, Chalong
items.blurb: A homey spot on Wichit Songkram Road near the Kathu junction on the way to Patong. Several set menus to match your budget, from a small set up to the larger 'Suk Samran' set with more on it — pick by group size.
items.meta: Wichit Songkram Road · on the way to Patong

items.name: Little Seoul
items.blurb: All-you-can-eat Korean BBQ in the low three hundreds a head, with Korean-style marinated meats, banchan side dishes and Korean menu items to choose from. Good if you want unlimited Korean without paying a premium.

items.name: Yakiniku Villa 3
items.blurb: Korean–Japanese grill buffet with no time limit, open late. There's soy-marinated prawns, river prawns, sushi, sashimi and several cuts of meat. Good for a long meal when you get back late after a day out.
items.price: Several tiers by set · check in store

items.name: Sukishi Korean Charcoal Grill (Central Festival Phuket)
items.blurb: Korean BBQ in the mall on the 3rd floor of Central Festival, with several buffet tiers, boldly marinated Korean-style meats and lots of side dishes. The afternoon Happy Hour usually has a special price. Good for families who'd rather eat in the mall with the air-con on.
items.meta: Central Festival, 3rd floor · in the mall

items.name: Shabu Lion — Premium Shabu & Japanese Buffet
items.blurb: Premium Japanese shabu and grill in the Talad Nuea area on Phuket Town Road, with several grades from Standard up to Platinum, which adds wagyu and salmon sashimi. Good if you want to upgrade the ingredients but still keep costs in check with the entry-level set.

items.name: Phuket Seafood Buffet
items.blurb: The most affordable way into a seafood buffet here — prawns, shellfish, crab and fish to choose from, with about two hours at the table. Good if you want to try a seafood buffet without spending big.
items.price: Adults around ฿299 · kids ฿159 (drinks not included)

items.name: Bubbles Restaurant — Grand Mercure Phuket Patong
items.blurb: Seafood buffet at a Patong hotel with a full spread of seafood and a nice setting. There's often a 'pay for 3, get 4' deal and no time limit. Good for a celebration meal, or for a bigger group splitting the deal to bring the per-head cost down.

blocks.title: How to get the best value
blocks.html: Hotel restaurants (like Bubbles, Cafe Andaman, Sea Breeze) tend to run their seafood buffet only on certain days or for certain seatings, and often have a 'pay for 3, get 4' deal. Go as a group and check the deals ahead of time and it works out a lot cheaper per head. The cheapest charcoal mookata sits outside the tourist areas — the trade-off is a short ride out.

blocks.text: Which to pick, by budget and occasion

items.name: On a budget, just with friends
items.blurb: Heng Heng / Super Heng / Chalong Buffet, from just over a hundred to three hundred a head. Charcoal and the dome pan, easy to settle in for a long sit.

items.name: Craving Korean or Japanese
items.blurb: Little Seoul / Yakiniku Villa 3 / Sukishi / Shabu Lion — good marinated meats with sushi and sashimi on the side, great for friends and family.

items.name: A celebration, all about seafood
items.blurb: Phuket Seafood Buffet (an easy starting price) or Bubbles at the Patong hotel — prawns, shellfish, crab and fish in full, with a nice setting.

blocks.text: Hotel seafood buffets that run on set nights

blocks.html: Beyond the places open every day, Phuket also has hotel seafood buffets that only run on certain nights. The seafood tends to be fresher and more generous, the trade-off being a higher price and the need to book ahead. Good for a night when you want one fancy meal.

items: Cafe Andaman (Cape Panwa Hotel) — Friday-night seafood grill with big tiger prawns and several cuts of meat, around ฿800/person (drinks not included), out in the Cape Panwa area.
Sea Breeze Cafe & Terrace — seafood buffet on certain days only (e.g. Tuesday/Saturday), around ฿999/person, with a wide range of seafood and good service.
Bubbles (Grand Mercure Patong) — seafood buffet with no time limit, around ฿1,399/person, with a 'pay for 3, get 4' deal that's great for a group.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Prices and the days they run at hotel restaurants change with the tourist seasons all the time. In high season (Nov–Apr) they tend to be pricier and you'll need to book; charcoal mookata prices are fairly steady by comparison. Always call ahead or message the restaurant's page before you set out.

blocks.text: What to know before a buffet in Phuket

items: Many places put a clock on your table — Korean and Japanese grill in the malls usually gives you around 1.5–2 hours, while a lot of charcoal mookata places have no time limit. Check first if you plan to sit a while.
Are drinks charged separately? — most mookata places include water and soft drinks, but plenty of seafood buffets charge extra for drinks.
Leftovers usually get charged — most buffets add a fee if you take food and don't finish it, so take a little at a time and go back for more.
Can you get there? — the cheaper mookata places tend to sit outside the tourist areas, so if you don't have a vehicle, budget for a taxi or motorbike taxi to get out there.

faq.q: What's the cheapest mookata buffet in Phuket?
faq.a: Classic charcoal dome-pan places start at around 149–199 THB per person — for example Heng Heng Mookata (around 149 THB, drinks included) and Super Heng (around 195 THB, no time limit). Most sit outside the main tourist areas, which is why they're cheaper than the mall or hotel spots.

faq.q: How much does a seafood buffet in Phuket start at?
faq.a: If you want to try one on a budget, Phuket Seafood Buffet runs around 299 THB for adults and 159 THB for kids (drinks not included), open in the evenings. Hotel seafood buffets like Bubbles in Patong are around 1,399 THB per person, but often have a 'pay for 3, get 4' deal.

faq.q: Where should I go for all-you-can-eat Korean BBQ in Phuket?
faq.a: Little Seoul at around 330 THB is a good-value pick. Yakiniku Villa 3 is open late (roughly 11:30am–11:30pm) with marinated prawns, sushi and sashimi. Sukishi on the 3rd floor of Central Festival is good for eating in the mall with the air-con on, and usually has a Happy Hour deal in the afternoon.

faq.q: Do hotel buffets need a booking ahead of time?
faq.a: It's best to book, because hotel seafood buffets like Cafe Andaman (Cape Panwa) or Sea Breeze tend to run only on certain nights — Fridays, Tuesdays or Saturdays, for example — and seats fill fast in high season. Call to check the days and the latest prices before you go.

faq.q: Do Phuket buffets put a time limit on you, and do you pay extra for leftovers?
faq.a: Korean and Japanese grill in the malls usually caps you at around 1.5–2 hours, while a lot of charcoal mookata places have no time limit. Almost every buffet has a policy of charging extra if you take food and don't finish it, so take a little at a time and go back for more.
